history.summary: Freehold 1BR at Royce Residences (D14) for $1.08M / $1475 PSF, with a high algo score (814) but only 8 URA transactions, no district median PSF, and an oversized-for-1BR 732 sqft footprint. The thin-data boutique profile and weak fundamentals behind the score push this to Neutral-to-Avoid; I rate Avoid on data unreliability.
history.rating_rationale: Only 8 URA transactions and a null median PSF mean both the 5.9%/yr rate and any value judgement are unreliable. 732 sqft for a 1BR is unusually large (oversized — the low $1475 PSF is partly a size artefact), $1.08M for a 1BR is a thin resale segment, and Kallang MRT is a 810m/10-min walk. The 814 score rests on cheap freehold PSF over a big unit, not on liquidity or verified appreciation — exactly the thin-data boutique the rubric says to avoid.

history.summary: A small freehold Geylang unit asking $1,475 psf — well above the project's own ~$1,222 psf 12-month average. The algo's -20.4% 'cheap-for-age' signal is contradicted by real building transactions; this unit is priced rich, not cheap.
history.rating_rationale: Asking $1,475 psf sits far above Royce's own trailing-12-month average of ~$1,222 psf, and the dossier itself flags psf_above_market with a +13.2% premium vs the size cohort (on just 2 cohort txns). The -20.4% age-adjusted 'cheap' score is a district-baseline artifact that does not survive a building-level check — the strongest robust forward signal (genuinely cheap vs verified recent comps) is absent here. Appreciation 3.7% is only a regional baseline (8 txns, no real CAGR), so there is no value AND no momentum support. The 732 sqft unit is the largest/'1+study' type in a 40-unit boutique block, fine physically, but D14 Geylang carries a real red-light-district stigma that drags exit liquidity. Freehold is not a forward edge per v3.4 priors. Paying a premium for a small unit in a stigma-adjacent micromarket with thin cohort data is the wrong side of the value trade.
